action.message:
Diagnosis: In parse_binding's except Error branch (parser.py:169-176), recovery uses `_rest_of_line = r"[^
]*(?:|
|
)?"`. The alternation tries `` first, so on a CRLF it consumes only the ``, leaving the `
` for the next binding. That stray `
` becomes the invalid binding's original.string ending in `` (not the full CRLF), and the following GOOD=ok binding starts at line 2 but its original.string is prefixed by the leftover `
`, so it isn't exactly "GOOD=ok
".

Change plan: Reorder the alternation to `(?:
|
|)?` so CRLF is matched as one unit, mirroring `_newline`/`_end_of_line`. This keeps LF and lone-CR behavior identical and preserves repeated invalid lines. No other files change.

tool_call.name: finish

The alternation tries `\\r` first, so on a CRLF it consumes only the `\\r`, leaving the `\\n` for the next binding. That stray `\\n` becomes the invalid binding's original.string ending in `\\r` (not the full CRLF), and the following GOOD=ok binding starts at line 2 but its original.string is prefixed by the leftover `\\n`, so it isn't exactly \"GOOD=ok\\n\".\n\nChange plan: Reorder the alternation to `(?:\\r\\n|\\n|\\r)?` so CRLF is matched as one unit, mirroring `_newline`/`_end_of_line`. This keeps LF and lone-CR behavior identical and preserves repeated invalid lines. No other files change.", "summary": "Diagnose CRLF recovery bug and propose regex fix"}
